we propose a novel framework to integrate deep shape representations into classical least squares optimization problems for simultaneous localization and mapping, and show that the resulting model outperforms both the classical and the deep end to end approaches.

we show that classical optimization based methods can be improved by the inclusion of higher dimensional object shape representations, while at the same time we demonstrate that deep learning based methods can be extended by the inclusion of more classical photometric and geometric consistency terms, which are known to be crucial for robust and accurate dense reconstruction.
we are the first work to embed deep shape priors into the classical iterative least squares framework for simultaneous localization and mapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep shape priors can be successfully embedded in traditional least squares optimization problems, and thus can potentially be applied to a variety of other problems in computer vision.
classical optimization based SLAM algorithms are not only able to benefit from modern deep learning models, but also to provide the latter with a more accurate and robust environment model.
the combination of classical and modern approaches can lead to a significant increase in mapping performance, and we hope that it will inspire future works in the field to follow the same path.
